One declaration in the stylesheet, and one abstraction in the test file that every stylesheet pin in it then uses — so that at the end of this change there is no second CSS parser left in the suite. Plus the one-line repair that makes the suite green so any of it can be verified. The diagnosis is settled and this round does not reopen it; the corrections are to the executable QA steps, to three acceptance artefacts that disagreed with each other, and to four citations and wordings.

R1 — THE QA BOOT IS FIXED SO THE BROWSER HALF MEASURES SOMETHING. The scratch DB_PATH prefix goes on BOTH `sdlc:seed` and `sdlc:serve`. As the proposal's own evidence records, with the prefix on the serve command alone the seed wrote ./data/app.db and the server read a 4096-byte schema-only scratch file, so every `scrollWidth == innerWidth` check in AC-2 and AC-10 passed on a page with no awaiting list at all — and posting a valid decision did not help, because the API does not create a tenant row, `firstTenant()` at src/web/pages.js:31-33 takes `tenants.list()[0]` and returns null, and `decisionsOf` at pages.js:614-619 returns []. The boot assertion now checks what is actually being distinguished — the scratch file is not schema-only AND the page carries `class="awaiting-list"` AND a non-zero `data-decision-id` count AND the seeded id — and it DROPS the exact 225280-byte figure. That number was a maintenance liability of exactly the kind the plan removed from AC-3, and it sat on the one step QA runs first and stops on; one more seeded row anywhere moves it and the failure message would be about bytes rather than about a database that did not seed.

R2 — THE POST BODY IN QA STEP 2 IS SPECIFIED IN FULL AND CAN NOW EXECUTE. src/domain/decisions.js:246 requires four arrays — `evidence_refs`, `memory_refs`, `model_versions`, `prompt_versions` — and the step named two of them; it was rejected 400 MISSING_DO_NOTHING on `model_versions` before anything was written. The step now names all four, gives the exact curl that ASSIGNS `$RESPONSE` before the `sed` that reads it (the previous text captured from a variable nothing ever set, so the pass condition grepped for the empty string and matched every line of the page), and posts with `tenant_id: tenant_demo` explicitly. That last part is mine, not either document's: `resolveTenantId` at src/api/routes.js:118-124 returns a caller-supplied string verbatim, so a QA agent who pastes any other tenant id creates a SECOND tenant and repoints the page's `firstTenant()` — the exact exposure the new test guards against in its own fixture, live in the QA boot. The render half's fixture was already specified in full (R2 in the proposal, verified by both prior rounds) and stands: the eight-field `repos.decisions.create(...)` returns `{created: true}` and the two-field form raises `TypeError: Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 3`, because src/data/db.js:123-134 declares nine `TEXT NOT NULL` columns and src/data/repositories.js:344-352 binds nine values. The citation is corrected to 344-352; the plan's 342-350 stopped one short of the ninth.

R3 — AC-2, AC-10 AND QA STEP 3 NOW NAME THE SAME SET. AC-2 required `scrollWidth === innerWidth` on six surfaces including /approvals with no exception, while AC-10 named `li.approval-card` on /approvals as the one exception this change does not fix and qa_script step 3 said 'assert the invariant everywhere else'. This is the same defect class the last two rejections were sent back for, in a place this round had not looked, and the whole point of writing the exception three times in one order is that it is written three times.

R4 — AC-5 SAYS IT IS NOT MACHINE-OBSERVED, BECAUSE IT IS NOT. The twelve-step mutation matrix is run by a person against the shipped stylesheet, with the file reverted between each. `npm run sdlc:verify` cannot see it and no browser can; the proposal calls it 'the only automated evidence' while also conceding it is 'a specification plus prior prototypes, not a run', and both sentences cannot stand. The criterion now says so and names who runs the twelve verdicts and where they are written down. Note what IS automated and what is not: contract case 8 is the prelude-mangling string, contract case 9 is the nested-override shape, and the new pin's non-empty collection assertion is mutation 1's mechanism, so the READER's three dangerous failure modes are already covered by fixture strings in CI; what only a person can run is the integration of that reader against the real file. The critique's proposed remedy — set `verify: "review"` — is not available: the enum is browser | test | api.

R5 — THE `.panel strong` JUSTIFICATION IS CORRECTED TO WHAT IS TRUE. styles.css:195 is `.panel h2` and `grep 'panel strong' src/web/styles.css` returns nothing; the critique is right that there is no such rule today. But the claim it supports is sound: `.panel h2` IS a panel-descendant rule, which is what makes panel-descendant styling the house idiom, and the step's mechanism (the appended rule governs the strong, the strong is a grid item of the li, so its min-content floors the li again, and neither the new pin nor the card pin fires) is unaffected. The wording now says `.panel h2` is the idiom precedent and that `.panel strong` is the form an author would reach for, not a rule that is there.

A. Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere;` to the EXISTING `.awaiting-list li` rule in src/web/styles.css, in place among its display / gap / border / border-radius / padding declarations, with one comment in the same voice and for the same reason as the wrap rule at styles.css:385-393: a grid item is floored at its min-content width, the decision_id is free text, `anywhere` rather than `break-word` because break-word creates the break opportunity but leaves intrinsic sizing alone. NOT as a second rule with the same selector — the new pin's conflict check would read the fix as an override of itself.

B. Add four shared helpers near the top of test/web/pages.test.js, beside H1_HOOK (line 23) and mainOf (line 37), and route all eight stylesheet read sites through them. Only the plumbing moves, with the single R3-of-the-proposal exception (the ch-only narrowing) named explicitly.

  `readStylesheet()` — the single readFileSync of src/web/styles.css, returning the SOURCE STRING. Every one of the eight sites becomes `const css = readStylesheet();` — the shape they have today — and the parse is one call on top. It returns the string rather than the parsed rules on purpose: the card pin's and the tenant pin's `length > 0` guards and failure messages are about the file, and the forced-colors pin's source-order assertion is easiest to read against the text it is ordering. This also makes AC-9's grep mean exactly what it says.

  `cssRules(source)` — strip /* */ with the SAME expression the card pin uses today at line 1696 (`css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, ' ')`), then walk with a brace stack. A frame whose selector starts with '@' is a BLOCK whose children are rules; any other frame is a rule whose body is declarations. ';' terminates a declaration inside a rule and a prelude inside an at-rule. Nested rules are emitted with their own selector and a nested flag meaning 'not at top level'. At-rule frames are not emitted. Every rule carries a source index. TWO FAILURE MODES PRODUCE PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT AND NEITHER SHOWS UP UNTIL A PIN DEPENDS ON IT: accumulating the prelude through a rule body concatenates `width: 100vw;` onto the selector of the next nested rule, and a reader that appends nested text to the parent body instead of descending into it drops every nested rule and reinstates the at-rule blind spot exactly — while passing every test in the file as written today. This order pins NO magic rule count: a total breaks on every future stylesheet edit for no semantic reason and would not have caught either, because a reader that mangles nested selectors can still return the right number and one that drops nested rules can still return a different right number.

  `declarations(body, prop)` — one property's values from an already comment-stripped body, anchored on a declaration boundary (start of body, or after a ';') rather than a bare substring, with a trailing chunk after the last ';' treated as a declaration. THE REASONS FOR THE ANCHORING ARE MEASURED, NOT ELEGANT, and one common reason is false: 'min-width' is NOT a substring of 'min-height'. The reasons that are real, both green today: (a) a rule with no min-width at all but a comment naming one reads as ['16ch'], count 1, GREEN — the BUG-1 state passing the BUG-1 pin, because the min-width pin does not strip comments while the card pin beside it does; (b) a comment standing beside a real declaration is consumed as the declaration, so widths comes back ['0','16ch'] where the real floor is 16ch. The third thing the boundary buys is the custom-property case: a bare substring search matches `--min-width: 16ch` and a boundary-anchored one does not, in a stylesheet whose `:root` declares seventeen custom properties. The trailing-chunk clause is a STATED LOOSENING, not a repair: dropping the trailing semicolon from `.page-title`'s `line-height: 1.25` is GREEN by design while dropping it from `#main > *`'s `min-width: 0` stays RED because the existing regexes require the ';'. Nothing is silently removed; the file shouts, and tests[] pins both directions.

  `conflictingOverrides(rules, pinned, selectors, prop)` — the card pin's override loop, lifted out of that test's body and corrected. The property is a fourth argument and the filter `declarations(other.body, prop).length > 0` runs inside, because the card pin's existing /overflow-wrap\s*:/ filter is what makes the comment above it true — a rule that cannot override the card classes does not turn the suite red. Take the property away and you get one of two failures: drop the filter and a narrow-viewport padding tweak on a pinned selector turns the suite red for a declaration that cannot change the property, re-breaking a tolerance #71 added on purpose; or hardcode overflow-wrap inside and the non-wrap pins get a check that can never fire. `pinned` is the rule or the SET of rules the calling pin has already asserted on, and every member is exempt — the new pin's collection is a set, and without the exemption the fix is reported as an override of itself. A conflict is reported for any rule other than the pinned set, at ANY source index, top-level or nested, declaring `prop` on a comma-split selector part equal to a member of `selectors`. Symmetric in source order, because an override authored above the pinned rule wins at narrow viewports exactly as one below does, and the shipped forced-colors carve-out is the one existing case of that shape.

  THE SELECTOR LOOKUP MUST ANCHOR ON THE SELECTOR'S END — compare a comma-split part to the pinned selector with `===`, never `selector.includes(pinnedSelector)`. '.opportunity-roww' and '.tenant-names' both contain their pinned selector as a substring; the current `\s*\{` anchors give the pins their rename protection today, and a substring lookup deletes it across all eight pins at once, invisibly.

  WHERE THE CONFLICT CHECK IS CALLED, and this is the design decision that matters most. Call it at the card pin (1691) and at the new .awaiting-list pin ONLY. 1652 (#main > *), 1663 (.table-scroll), 1756 (.approval-actions), 1766 (.approval-actions input), 1801 (.journal-drawer-body) and 1818 (.tenant-name) each already collect EVERY rule matching their selector and assert the property on every one of them, so their every-match loop IS the same coverage a same-selector conflict check would give — and because the helper exempts the pinned set, and the pinned set on those six is every rule that could ever match, the call can never fire there. It is dead code that reads as coverage. Put one line in each of those six tests' comments saying the every-match loop is that selector's override check, so the absence reads as a decision. Add one contract case distinguishing a pin whose pinned set is the whole selector from one whose pinned set is a single rule, so the distinction cannot rot silently.

  TWO PINS THAT ARE NOT MECHANICAL. `.page-title` (1632) asserts EVERY .page-title rule rather than the first: an appended `.page-title { margin: 4rem }` is green under a first-match check and the page breaks. `#main:focus` (344) needs an exact count, not a conflict check, because the conflict check is genuinely unavailable there: its one later same-selector rule IS the intentional forced-colors carve-out, so any same-selector override check reports it by design. The count pin — exactly one top-level #main:focus rule declaring `outline: none`, and exactly one not at top level carrying the carve-out — goes on THAT test of the two, stated here so the implementer does not have to choose.

  THE FORCED-COLORS PIN, the third place that needs care, and the loosening is accepted on purpose and pinned. The current regex at pages.test.js:360 is /@media\s*\(forced-colors:\s*active\)\s*\{[^@]*?#main:focus\s*\{([^}]*)\}/, and its `[^@]*?` means it only finds the carve-out when it is the first thing in the block. The reader finds it wherever it sits, so the rewrite is strictly MORE PERMISSIVE. The assertions that carry the meaning are unchanged — the carve-out exists, declares `outline: 2px solid CanvasText`, and comes after the bare #main:focus rule at equal specificity, both selectors being 1,1,0 — and a mutation that puts another nested rule before the carve-out must still pass, so the loosening is a stated behaviour. The test's comment says the parser's strictness changed, not the assertion. Keep the `length > 0` guard on the not-at-top-level lookup specifically, so a reader regression that stopped descending into at-rules cannot make this test pass vacuously on a file with no carve-out at all. The source-order assertion at pages.test.js:372-377 is the only thing in the suite that pins WHY the carve-out wins, and its comment says so; it must survive the rewrite as a comparison of the two rules' SOURCE INDICES rather than of character offsets, deliberately, not by accident.

  THE NEW .awaiting-list li PIN, in the house style of #main > * and .tenant-name rather than a whole-body assertion, and in ONE test. In order: (a) collect every rule that is NOT nested, whose comma-split selector part is `.awaiting-list` or `.awaiting-list li`, and whose body declares overflow-wrap — the property filter is part of the COLLECTION predicate, not only inside the helper, and the test's comment must say that in those terms, because the media-nested rule's selector part IS exactly '.awaiting-list li' and an unfiltered collection takes it in, at which point deepEqual([], ['anywhere']) fails and the suite goes red for a padding declaration; (b) require the collection NON-EMPTY, with a message that says so, so deleting the declaration and leaving a comment is red; (c) require each collected rule's overflow-wrap values to deepEqual ['anywhere']; (d) run `conflictingOverrides(rules, collected, ['.awaiting-list', '.awaiting-list li', '.awaiting-list li strong', '.awaiting-list li span'], 'overflow-wrap')` and require it to report nothing. Today the file yields exactly one `.awaiting-list li` rule with zero overflow-wrap declarations in it, so (b) is what turns the current state red rather than vacuous. Two strictnesses with their costs recorded in out_of_scope: `.awaiting-list` (the ul) is in the collection's selector set, because `overflow-wrap` is inherited and the pin must not report a correct fix on the parent as absent; and the collection requires the declaration at TOP LEVEL, because a fix authored only inside `@media (max-width: 900px)` satisfies the new pin in full AND satisfies the whole browser sweep at 320 / 375 / 414, all of which are inside that query, while the defect is not inherently narrow-viewport.

  (e) the render half, in the same test, AS A LINK ASSERTION AND NOTHING MORE. Use `seededRepos(prefix)` — which creates tenant_demo and the seeded decisions — NOT bare `freshRepos()`, which has no tenant, and `decisionsOf` at src/web/pages.js:614-619 is `if (!tenant) { return []; }`, so the page renders the empty branch with no `class="awaiting-list"` anywhere. Before rendering, assert that `repos.tenants.list()` is exactly one row and its id is `tenant_demo`, with a message saying the fixture's tenant selection is load-bearing for `firstTenant()` — that assertion is what stops a future seed adding a second tenant from repointing the whole page, and it is the same check that proves a seeded database was served. Then create ONE further decision on top of the seed through the EIGHT-FIELD `repos.decisions.create(...)` of R2, whose decision_id is `'dec_' + 'q'.repeat(136)` (140 unbreakable characters), and assert that /journal at override 'partial' emits `class="awaiting-list"` and an `<li data-decision-id=...>` whose `<strong>` holds that id whole. WHAT THIS HALF PROVES, stated exactly so nobody reads it as more: that the id survives the DATA LAYER and the template untouched — it is not truncated, and it is not re-encoded. It says NOTHING about escaping, and the fixture could not prove that if it tried: 136 'q' characters contain nothing `escapeHtml` (src/web/pages.js:34-40) acts on, so the assertion would pass identically with `escapeHtml` deleted. The clause 'not escaped into something shorter' is therefore removed from the assertion and from the comment. The corollary for anyone changing the fixture: a decision_id containing `&`, `<`, `>` or `"` reaches the page ESCAPED, and the 'holds that id whole' assertion would then fail with a message about a missing id rather than about the fixture. The assertion is NOT a measurement of layout and must not be described as one: the renderer reads no stylesheet — the shell links it at pages.js:68 and the asset route serves it at src/api/routes.js:263 — this repository has no browser driver, and this half passes with or without the declaration. validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The critique returned 'flawed' with ten findings, two blocking. I re-ran the load-bearing ones myself rather than accepting them, upheld seven, partly upheld two, dismissed one, and found a defect in the proposal that the critique never looked for. The design survives; the corrections are to the executable steps, to three acceptance artefacts that contradicted each other, and to four citations and wordings. This is not a tidy consensus and I am not presenting it as one.

WHAT THE CRITIQUE GOT RIGHT, AND IT GOT THE BEST THING IN THE ROUND RIGHT TWICE. The first blocking finding is a defect seven rounds of self-checking missed: qa_script step 2 names two of the four arrays src/domain/decisions.js:246 requires, so the step is rejected 400 MISSING_DO_NOTHING on `model_versions` before anything is written — and the step whose entire purpose was the R2 fixture correction was the one step that could not run. The same step then captures `DEC_ID` out of `$RESPONSE`, a variable no instruction in it ever assigns, so its pass condition greps for the empty string and matches every line of the page. I read the validator and the route myself. The second blocking finding is the same defect class the last two rejections were sent back for, in a place this round had not looked: AC-2 required `scrollWidth === innerWidth` on six surfaces including /approvals with no exception, while AC-10 and qa_script step 3 both carved `li.approval-card` out, so a correct implementation could satisfy AC-10 and fail AC-2. Both are fixed in the order above and the three now name the same set. I added a third defect in the same step that neither document found: the step posts without a `tenant_id`, and `resolveTenantId` returns a caller-supplied string verbatim, so a QA agent who pastes any other id creates a second tenant and repoints the page's `firstTenant()` while every other assertion still passes. That is the new test's guarded fixture exposure, live and unguarded in the QA boot.

WHERE I DISAGREE WITH THE CRITIQUE, and the disagreement is about the shape of the ticket. Its third major finding is that the issue's seventh review finding calls the helper extraction 'Optional, and not worth blocking on' and the plan never quotes or answers that. The review that wrote that sentence took its own advice for each of the four findings it filed: the min-width fix is 'accept only ch', the two comment findings' fix is 'reuse the card pin's strip... a consistency fix rather than new machinery', and the at-rule finding offers a cheaper alternative that is also not the extraction. 'Optional' was about the EXTRACTION as the vehicle for findings that were not optional at all. Against that: the new pin needs a stylesheet parse, and building it on a fresh local parser inside one test adds a fifth parser to a file with four hand-rolled ones — a net increase in the class this ticket exists to close — and the product fix is one declaration that ships whether or not the migration does, so nothing about the layout bug waits. What waits is closing two pins that are false green today. I considered `scope_changed` to maintainer and rejected it: a split puts one line of CSS in a different ticket from the parser that pins it, which is how the false 'measured and safe' entry that started this whole chain got written. I also rejected the middle path — the review's own two targeted fixes without the migration — because it closes two of the four false greens and leaves a measured 1371px overflow open, then adds a new pin that must parse correctly anyway. The plan's own risk record on the unexecuted migration is honest, and I am not going to answer a real risk by making the plan smaller.
